facts: Parse the user-facing flag string once so validation and process spawning see the same argv. Quotes group whitespace but are not passed to ripgrep because spawn() does not invoke a shell.

A `cwd` naming a file asks for that file's matches, so search it from its directory instead of failing to start in it. Never through a broker: a sponsored run's broker admits only the directory search below, and must not be preceded by a stat of a path the model chose.
Do not deduplicate: repeated flag-argument pairs such as `-g *.ts` are meaningful. The shared parser keeps quoted values as one argv entry.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: code-search-flags
entries.summary: Shared/Core, SDK changes across 3 file(s) (+116/−42).

ai.title: Relocate code search flag parser to common, support file cwd
ai.summary: The shared flag parser was moved from the SDK to the common package to ensure validation and process spawning use the same argv in both normal and sponsored runs. The code search tool now detects when the working directory parameter names a file and searches from that file's directory instead of failing. This file-specific search is skipped when a process broker is active to prevent unauthorized path stats in sponsored environments. Sponsored sandbox imports were updated to consume the parser from its new location in common.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `parseCodeSearchFlags` to `common/src/util/code-search-flags.ts` and removes the duplicate from `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts`; `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` updates its import to source the function from `common`.
ai.unknowns: The specific consumer of the relocated parser in the CLI surface is not shown in this diff, only the SDK and common package changes are visible.

changes.what: Added the shared flag parser utility to the common package.
Removed the local parser implementation and added file-path handling for the working directory parameter.
Updated imports to use the shared flag parser from the common package.

eli5.text: The tool that searches your project files for text is now moved into the shared core of the application so that it behaves exactly the same in normal coding sessions and in sponsored runs. It can now search a single file directly instead of failing when told to start in a file, but only in normal sessions; sponsored runs still cannot do this to keep the advertiser's environment safe. This is internal plumbing work that makes the search more consistent and reliable, but it does not change what you see or how you use the assistant day-to-day.

entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+6/−0).

ai.title: Add paid signup destination analytics events
ai.summary: Three analytics event constants were added to the `AnalyticsEvent` enum in the `common` package to track paid signup destination journeys. The new events are `FREEBUFF_START_VIEWED`, `FREEBUFF_START_SIGN_IN_CLICKED`, and `FREEBUFF_START_SIGNED_IN`, which map to the string values `freebuff.start_viewed`, `freebuff.start_sign_in_clicked`, and `freebuff.start_signed_in`. The accompanying comment clarifies that a handoff arrival is not a signup and directs analysts to compare the signed-out entry with canonical `web.signup` and `message_sent` conversions.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, the diff adds three new enum members (`FREEBUFF_START_VIEWED`, `FREEBUFF_START_SIGN_IN_CLICKED`, `FREEBUFF_START_SIGNED_IN`) with a comment block describing them as 'Paid signup destinations'.
ai.unknowns: The specific UI surface that emits these events is not shown in the diff, only the event definitions and their intended comparison logic.

eli5.text: Freebuff added three new measurement labels to its internal tracking system to follow the path of a person who arrives at a specific page meant to set up a paid account. These new labels are currently just defined in the code and are not yet connected to any screens, so the actual tracking of these page visits has not started yet. This change is for the team that builds Freebuff and allows them to distinguish between simply landing on a sign-up page and successfully completing a login, but it causes no visible change for you today.

testNames: shows a fallback when validation refuses without error details

ai.title: Surface agent validation transport errors in CLI chat
ai.summary: Agent validation transport failures now block message sending and display the specific error reason in the CLI chat instead of silently aborting with an empty error list. The useAgentValidation hook no longer filters out network errors, and the sendMessage hook elevates validation failures from warnings to error-level telemetry while injecting a descriptive error message into the chat transcript. The SDK validation layer includes the HTTP status code in remote error messages for clearer diagnostics.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/hooks/use-agent-validation.ts, the validate callback now assigns validationResult.validationErrors directly to state instead of filtering them, and returns a constructed error object in the catch block. In cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts, the validation failure block replaces a logger.warn call with logger.error and injects a createErrorChatMessage containing the first error's message into the chat history. In sdk/src/validate-agents.ts, the remote validation error message format changed to include the HTTP status code explicitly.

changes.what: Agent validation hook retains transport error details instead of filtering them out
Message send hook surfaces validation failures as chat error messages and error-level telemetry
Remote agent validation includes HTTP status code in error messages

eli5.text: When the assistant checks your custom agent settings before you send a message, it now shows the specific reason for any failure directly in the chat instead of silently blocking the send. This affects anyone who writes custom agent instructions and uses the terminal or desktop app. You will now see a clear error message telling you exactly what went wrong, so you can fix the issue and try again without wondering why your message disappeared.

ai.title: Update read files tool description for image support
ai.summary: The description of the `legacyInputSchema` in `read-files.ts` now states that the tool reads text files and views images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP), noting that local image reads attach the image for visual inspection rather than returning bytes as text. The example input for the tool call was updated to include `screenshot.png` alongside `file.ts`. These prompt text updates align the schema description with the image handling capability introduced in the previous commit [dedd70d5], ensuring the model is instructed on how to interpret image files.
ai.evidence: The diff updates the `legacyInputSchema` description and example in `common/src/tools/params/tool/read-files.ts` to include image formats (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) and change the example input from `['path/to/file1.ts', 'path/to/file2.ts']` to `['path/to/file.ts', 'path/to/screenshot.png']`.

eli5.text: The written instructions given to the AI assistant now explain that it can look at picture files like screenshots, not just read words from code files. This is an internal improvement to the assistant's documentation; because the picture-reading ability was added in an earlier update, this change simply updates the guide so the assistant knows how to handle those images. You will not notice a difference in how the app runs today, but it helps the AI understand images you share with it.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: axiom-only-log
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+20/−1).

ai.title: Add message classification fields to ad telemetry allowlists
ai.summary: The Axiom-only log schemas in the common package now include message classification metadata for Flash pCTR operations. Two fields, `message_classification_lookup` and `message_classification_age_s`, were added to the `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` allowlist to record the status and age of the conversation's newest message classification. Additionally, `decisions_pctr_message_classification` was added to `ADS_FIRST_PARTY_DECISION_FIELDS` to indicate whether that classification block was included in the Flash pCTR batch. These content-free fields track operational states like `ready`, `missing`, `opted_out`, and `omitted` without carrying user identifiers or conversation content.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, the diff adds `message_classification_lookup` and `message_classification_age_s` to `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS`, and `decisions_pctr_message_classification` to `ADS_FIRST_PARTY_DECISION_FIELDS`.
ai.unknowns: The specific runtime implementation that populates these new Axiom fields is not shown in this diff.

eli5.text: The internal logging system for the ad-serving engine now records two new pieces of operational detail: whether the latest message in a conversation was successfully classified for ad relevance, and whether that classification was included in the batch sent to the ad model. This change is for the people who run and monitor the Freebuff service; it does not alter how ads appear to you or how you use the coding assistant. There is no visible effect or action needed for end users or developers.
